scenes.title: Getting started
scenes.learning_objective: Define gradient descent on quadratic loss f(x)=x squared using the derivative and learning rate to update a parameter.
scenes.narration_text: Gradient descent adjusts a parameter to reduce a loss. For our quadratic loss, square the parameter to measure error. The gradient is twice the parameter. Subtract the learning rate times this gradient at each update.

scenes.title: Following the changes
scenes.learning_objective: Interpret the tangent slope of quadratic loss and a downhill parameter update on the parabola.

visual_timeline.narration_text: The parabola has its minimum at zero.
Starting at three gives loss nine and positive slope six.
A suitable step against that slope moves left toward the minimum, reducing the loss.

scenes.title: Making connections
scenes.learning_objective: Compute one gradient descent update from initial x=3 with learning_rate=0.2, obtaining x=1.8 and loss=3.24.

visual_timeline.narration_text: Choose learning rate zero point two.
Multiply it by six to get one point two.
Subtract that from three: the new parameter is one point eight.
Squaring it gives loss three point two four.

scenes.narration_text: Choose learning rate zero point two. Multiply it by six to get one point two. Subtract that from three: the new parameter is one point eight. Squaring it gives loss three point two four.

scenes.title: Putting it together
scenes.learning_objective: Summarize gradient descent: recompute the gradient, apply a suitable learning rate, and monitor convergence through the loss.
scenes.narration_text: In summary, recompute the gradient after each update and monitor the loss. Step size matters; oversized steps can fail to improve it. Stop when gradients and improvements become sufficiently small.
